mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) over the previous six months indicates strong consumer demand, which drives corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where RSAFS shows sustained increase over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points, signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200k and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) over the previous three months indicates a strong demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator for economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST shows sustained increase over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% over the previous quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 decreases by more than 0.5% in 1 quarter.
